summary: Payette NF lookout built in 1933 near McCall, Idaho; tower taken down in 2008, the cab moved to a McCall museum, and the residence cabin left at the site.

facts.design: 72-foot open steel tower with an Aermotor 7x7 cab, plus a log residence cabin
facts.agency: Payette National Forest (cooperator); the Central Idaho Historical Museum administers the register entry

access.note: The cab may be toured at the Central Idaho Historical Museum in McCall; no source describes access to the original site

facts.status_note: The tower was taken down in 2008. The cab is at the McCall museum; the residence cabin remains at the original site, per the Register.

resolved_conflicts.field: fate of the cab and tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and Idaho Fire Lookouts say the cab went to the museum; Idaho Fire Lookouts adds that the tower was sold and moved to Lewiston; a McCall visitor listing (allmccall.com) names only the Sloan Point cab. The story gives the Register's account and flags the museum listing.
firelookout.com describes the museum move as a hope; the Register and Idaho Fire Lookouts state the cab move as done. The story uses the later account and notes the difference.

notes_for_editor: The museum move of the cab is supported by the Register and Idaho Fire Lookouts, but no museum source names a Split Creek cab; the story flags this. Idaho Fire Lookouts says the tower went to Lewiston, which no other source read confirms. Elevation conflict: the Register gives 5,017 ft (1,529 m), Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 6628 ft; not used. The brief's events field ('None relocated...') is a note, not an event, so it was not used. A separate Selway-region 'Split Creek Point' lookout exists on the Idaho Fire Lookouts site (seen in a search snippet only, not read); keep the two records apart. The brief's source_pages point to a separate museum-site record, which may be a duplicate. No source read describes the original site today or whether it is open to the public. Used 6 page reads and 2 searches.
